tagline: Asia's surf capital quadrupled its visitors after rebuilding from Typhoon Odette — its boats are the last thing still waiting for the upgrade.
summary: Siargao rebounded from Typhoon Odette (Dec 2021) into the Philippines' fastest-growing island destination: 529,822 arrivals in 2023, up 323% on 2022. Everything that makes it famous is reached by boat — the Cloud 9 surf coast, the Naked–Daku–Guyam island-hop tripod off General Luna, Sohoton Cove in Bucas Grande, and the Dapa ↔ Surigao mainland lifeline — yet all of it runs on diesel bangkas and aging ferries exposed to Pacific weather. A post-typhoon rebuild inside a protected seascape is a rare design-in window for a clean, smooth, weather-resilient foiling fleet.

use_cases.title: The General Luna island-hop tripod, electrified
use_cases.body: Naked, Daku and Guyam islands sit 1–3 nm off General Luna and host the island's single highest-volume boat activity. Quiet, wake-free foiling shuttles replace the diesel bangka flotilla — same beloved loop, none of the fumes or pounding.

use_cases.title: Sohoton Cove day-loop (Bucas Grande)
use_cases.body: Dapa/General Luna to Socorro's Sohoton Cove — jellyfish lagoons and caves inside a capacity-managed natural park ~20 nm away — becomes a smooth sub-hour foiling run instead of a long, swell-exposed banca ride that cancels in rough weather.

use_cases.title: Dapa ↔ Surigao City mainland lifeline
use_cases.body: The mainland link carries residents, supplies and visitors on aging ferries and fastcraft across open water. A foiling service (near the Pioneer II range edge at ~58 nm routed; the 12–15-pax N35 Shuttle from 2027 is the natural scheduled platform) cuts crossing time and rides above the chop that cancels conventional sailings.

use_cases.title: Premium resort transfers
use_cases.body: Direct foiling arrivals to Nay Palad Hideaway and the General Luna resort jetties — the barefoot-luxury segment that already pays for seamlessness gets a silent, smooth signature arrival.

use_cases.title: Visayas–Siargao line-haul
use_cases.body: Cebu ↔ Siargao and Bohol ↔ Siargao (~150 nm each) as Quanta-LR hybrid line-hauls from H2 2026+ — linking the Visayas tourism mesh to Siargao without any destination charging infrastructure.

journeys.today: Diesel bangka day-tour flotilla; loud, smoky, and beach-launched — the experience everyone comes for, delivered on 50-year-old boat technology.
journeys.with_navier: A near-silent foiling hop of minutes per leg — the tripod loop becomes an all-day, on-demand shuttle with zero wake over the reef flats.

journeys.today: ~1.5–2 hr open-water banca run, frequently cancelled when the Pacific swell wraps in; many visitors skip it.
journeys.with_navier: A ~50-minute smooth foiling run above the swell — Sohoton converts from a gamble into a bookable everyday loop.

journeys.today: Conventional ferry/fastcraft sailings of 2–3+ hours, weather-fragile across the Hinatuan Passage approaches.
journeys.with_navier: A foiling crossing at 20+ kt cruise riding above the chop — note: ~58 nm routed puts this near the Pioneer II range edge; N35 Shuttle (2027) is the natural scheduled platform.

journeys.today: Limited flights into small Sayak airport, or a long multi-leg ferry chain via Surigao — capacity caps the island's growth.
journeys.with_navier: A direct ~150 nm Quanta-LR hybrid line-haul (H2 2026+) — a second artery into the island that needs no new infrastructure at either end.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The island's whole experience economy is a tight all-electric mesh: 1–3 nm tripod hops, ~8 nm resort runs, ~20 nm Sohoton day-loops — all deep inside the 70 nm envelope from a General Luna or Dapa charging base. The ~58 nm Dapa↔Surigao mainland leg fits but sits near the range edge and is flagged for coordinate-level confirmation before becoming a marquee scheduled run.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Cebu ↔ Siargao and Bohol ↔ Siargao (~150 nm) hybrid line-hauls from H2 2026+ connect Siargao to the Visayas mesh with no charging-infrastructure dependency; Manila direct (~480 nm) is feasible within the 700 nm commercial range but Cebu staging is the practical pattern.

competitive_landscape: Today's water is run by the General Luna bangka day-tour cooperatives, resort transfer boats, and conventional ferry/fastcraft operators on the Surigao ↔ Dapa mainland run — proof of constant, paying, boat-borne demand. The pain is structural: open Pacific exposure means swell-cancelled island hops and mainland crossings, diesel noise and wake inside a protected seascape, and a fleet largely rebuilt after Odette to the same old specification. That gap between a world-class destination and dated boats is the opportunity.
seasonality: Pacific-facing Siargao has two rhythms: the Aug–Nov habagat-driven swell season that powers Cloud 9 (surf demand peaks exactly when small-boat comfort is worst — foiling's flagship condition) and the calmer amihan window (Dec–Mar). The island sits in the typhoon belt (Odette, Dec 2021, is living memory); statutory PAGASA signal closures apply, and within open windows foiling smoothness materially extends comfortable operating days.
regulatory_note: Siargao and its surrounding waters are a declared protected area (Siargao Island Protected Landscape and Seascape), and Sohoton Cove operates capacity-managed entry — a clean-marine, low-wake mandate built into the destination. The post-Odette rebuild keeps specifications open for clean-fleet design-in. Vessel certification through MARINA; jetty access via Dapa port (PPA) and per-resort jetties; LGU tourism offices manage the island-hopping trade.
